skill.name: data-visualization
skill.description: Guides chart selection, color choices, annotations, and data storytelling for clear reports, dashboards, and presentations.
skill.summary: Create clearer charts with practical data visualization rules and examples.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown fence false positives, but the skill contains confirmed external command examples. The critical issue is the curl-to-sh installer on SKILL.md line 14, combined with explicit permission to run the external infsh CLI.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl | sh with package manager instructions or a manual download flow that verifies checksums before execution.

remediation.issue: The skill allows agents to run infsh commands that may send user data to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running infsh and document what data is transmitted to inference.sh apps.

remediation.issue: Examples include external skill installation commands through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Move related skill installation commands to a non-executable note and warn users to review packages before installation.

content.value_statement: Raw metrics can confuse readers when chart choices, colors, and labels are inconsistent. This skill helps users choose the right chart, format it clearly, and explain the insight.
actual_capabilities: Recommends chart types for time series, categories, rankings, distributions, correlations, and geographic data.
Explains chart design rules for axes, gridlines, labels, sorting, titles, and annotation placement.
Provides color palette guidance for sequential, diverging, categorical, and colorblind-safe charts.
Shows recipes for line charts, horizontal bar charts, KPI cards, heatmaps, and dark mode charts.
Frames charts with data storytelling patterns, including context, tension, resolution, and insight titles.
limitations: Executable examples require the inference.sh CLI and may require an account.
The skill gives visualization guidance but does not verify source data accuracy.
Remote app examples may send chart inputs or generated code to external services.
Examples focus on Python, Matplotlib, and HTML rendering, not every charting library.

use_cases.title: Build Executive Dashboards
use_cases.description: Create chart recommendations and KPI treatments for leadership reporting with clear titles and focused annotations.

use_cases.title: Improve Analysis Charts
use_cases.description: Convert exploratory tables into readable bar, line, scatter, heatmap, or distribution charts for stakeholder review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Presentations
use_cases.description: Design concise visuals that highlight the main insight and avoid misleading axes, colors, or chart types.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Chart Type
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this data relationship: [describe columns and goal]. Recommend the best chart type and explain which chart types to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Clear Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this dataset summary into a clear chart plan: [paste summary]. Include title, axes, labels, colors, and annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dashboard Visual Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dashboard visual set for [audience] using these metrics: [metrics]. Recommend chart types, layout order, and color rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Visualization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chart plan for clarity and possible misleading choices: [describe chart]. Identify issues and provide a revised version.

output_examples.input: A monthly revenue table with last year and this year values.
output_examples.output: Use a two-line time series chart. Highlight the current year, mute last year, label the final values, and title it with the growth insight.

output_examples.input: A traffic source breakdown with six categories and one clear winner.
output: Use a sorted horizontal bar chart.
Highlight the winning source and use neutral colors for the rest.
Add value labels because exact percentages matter.

output_examples.input: A weekly activity matrix by day and hour.
output_examples.output: Use a heatmap with readable hour and day labels, a sequential color scale, and annotations only where exact values matter.

best_practices: Start with the reader question, then choose the chart type that answers it directly.
Use one main highlight color and keep supporting data visually quiet.
Write titles that state the insight instead of naming the chart type.
anti_patterns: Using pie charts for many categories or values that need precise comparison.
Truncating bar chart axes in ways that exaggerate differences.
Adding decorative elements that do not help readers understand the data.

faq.question: Does this skill generate charts?
faq.answer: It provides chart recipes and examples that can generate charts through the inference.sh CLI when users choose to run them.

faq.question: Which chart types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers line charts, bar charts, heatmaps, KPI cards, scatter plots, histograms, treemaps, and several chart alternatives.

faq.question: Can it help with dashboard design?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend chart types, ordering, titles, labels, colors, and annotations for dashboard metrics.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes colorblind-safe palette guidance and recommends labels, contrast, and readable text sizes.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: The guidance is readable without services, but executable examples use the inference.sh CLI and external apps.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Do not send sensitive data to external chart execution services unless your organization has approved that workflow.
